tasks.spec:
You are a repo fix worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repo (/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory) at HEAD — edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly two paths: factory/outbox_push.py and tests/test_outbox_push.py. Nothing else. Never touch .git, never commit, never run git add; leave changes uncommitted.

CONTEXT — a live incident on 2026-08-05: an escalation card was filed whose text read 'Approve = PAUSE the 10am publish'. The owner had tapped Approve meaning 'go/proceed' on six consecutive cards that evening, tapped Approve by habit, and a wanted launch was unwound across three platforms. Owner order (verbatim): 'add a card polarity rule so approve never means stop.' The rule: on any card, Approve must map to the SAFE-FORWARD action the owner wants; a stop/hold/destructive action must ride Respond/FIX with a typed word, never the affirmative button.

CHANGE (in factory/outbox_push.py, inside tick() where the card/buzz values are built from an outbox row): add a polarity lint executed on the human-facing text (the composed title + body + the row's eli5). Case-insensitive detection of Approve mapped to a stop verb, covering at least these constructions: 'approve = <stop>', 'approve means <stop>', 'approve: <stop>', 'approve -> <stop>', 'approve to <stop>', '✅ approve — <stop>', where <stop> starts with any of: pause, stop, halt, hold, cancel, delete, remove, kill, unschedule, abort, revoke, suspend, disable, block, retract, withdraw (word-boundary match on the verb immediately following the mapping token, tolerant of whitespace and an intervening 'the'). On detection: do NOT create the card, do NOT send the ping or buzz, do NOT consume the row (no hash record, no offset advance — same non-consume discipline as a failed card sender); LOGGER.error with a message that teaches the fix, e.g.: "card polarity violation for %s line %d: Approve must never mean '%s' — rephrase so Approve is the safe-forward action and the stop rides Respond with a typed word (owner rule 2026-08-05)"; count it and make the tick exit nonzero (reuse the existing sender-failure exit-code convention, exit 3). The row author sees a red service and the exact reason every tick until the row is rephrased. Put the stop-verb list and mapping regex in module-level constants with a comment citing the owner rule and the 2026-08-05 incident.

TESTS (extend tests/test_outbox_push.py in its existing style): (a) a row whose eli5 contains 'Approve = pause the launch' => no ping, no card, row not consumed, exit 3, error names the verb and the rule; (b) 'Approve = PAUSE the 10am publish' (the real incident text, mixed case) also caught; (c) a healthy row whose text contains the word 'pause' NOT mapped to Approve (e.g., 'WHAT IT NEEDS: approve the catch-up actions; ops will pause the old timer') is NOT flagged and cards normally — the lint must not false-positive on stop verbs elsewhere in the text; (d) 'Approve to cancel the schedule' caught.

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root — all must pass): PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_outbox_push.py tests/test_outbox_push_buzz.py tests/test_outbox_push_stall.py -q -p no:cacheprovider && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check

HARD RULES: smallest diff, no behavior change for healthy rows, no reformatting, never invoke any network, model CLI, MCP, or skill, leave changes uncommitted — the harness exports the diff.
